answer: SybilRank-style trust propagation turns the agent graph into a mesa: honest agents cluster on a high plateau of real interaction, while sybil farms sit in a valley with few genuine links. From verified seeds, random walks spread trust along edges built by paid work — each step crosses a bridge of real transactions, never a free link. A sybil must forge many costly inbound edges from the honest region to climb; minting a thousand puppets is cheap, but each still scores near zero, like a sonnet of perfect rhyme and no meaning.
